reason: E2 provides direct evidence for B2 ordering driven by Al–Ni–Co interactions and its temperature dependence in AlxCoCrFeNi, supporting the thermodynamic drive. E1 supports kinetic control of phase selection in HEAs but does not specifically address sluggish diffusion delaying B2 ordering in this composition, leaving that premise only loosely supported.
premises: Strong negative mixing enthalpies between Al–Ni and Al–Co drive B2 ordering
The high-temperature BCC phase is thermodynamically metastable relative to B2 ordering
Sluggish diffusion in multicomponent alloys kinetically delays the ordering transformation
Controlled cooling rate modulates atomic diffusion and thus the extent of ordering
Slow cooling enables local chemical ordering and compositional partitioning into B2 and disordered BCC
